fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled template digits (e.g. 'H2147483648') are parsed by mrb_read_int into 64-bit mrb_int n and then truncated to int; n=2147483648 becomes count=-2147483648.

fine_trace.code: srcidx += unpack_hex(mrb, sptr, srclen - srcidx, result, count, flags);
fine_trace.note: For 'H'/'h' (PACK_DIR_HEX with PACK_FLAG_COUNT2) the truncated negative count is forwarded to unpack_hex without any validation.
count == -1 is expanded to slen*2, but any other negative count (e.g. -2147483648) passes through unchanged.
The unchecked negative count is used as the new string length, so mrb_str_new receives len < 0. Safety condition that should have held: count >= 0.
RSTR_EMBEDDABLE_P(len) is (len) <= RSTRING_EMBED_LEN_MAX; a negative len satisfies it, so the string is initialized as embedded with the negative length.
len is negative (-2147483648), so the sentinel write lands far before the embedded buffer, an out-of-bounds write (ASan: SEGV caused by WRITE at this line).
